I checked the draft sentence by sentence against the brand policy.

- **"Peppermint. Just peppermint leaves, nothing else."** This is an ingredient fact, and the policy allows product facts as written.
- **"Cool and clean after a big meal."** This describes how the tea tastes and feels. It doesn't say the tea aids digestion, settles the stomach or has any effect on the body, so it isn't a health claim. If it were reworded to something like "aids digestion" or "settles your stomach", it would become one.
- **"Certified organic by the Soil Association."** This is on the approved claims list.

There are no unsupported numbers, superlatives, guarantees, testimonials, urgency or green claims. This is a brand-owned product page, so no ad label is needed. The copy is short and specific, and it has none of the filler phrases from the style list. It can go out as written.
